column3: Like any place name: 去美国, 在美国. Add 人 for a person: 美国人 is an American. The first character alone stands for the country in words such as 美元 and 美军.
column7: My friend works in the United States.
column9: Like any place name: 去美國, 在美國. Add 人 for a person: 美國人 is an American. The first character alone stands for the country in words such as 美元 and 美軍.

column3: It works like any place name: 去日本, 在日本. 日本人 is a Japanese person, and the language is 日语 or 日文. Alone, 日 is a bound form that stands for Japan.
column6: Wǒ xià ge yuè qù Rìběn.
column7: I am going to Japan next month.
column9: It works like any place name: 去日本, 在日本. 日本人 is a Japanese person, and the language is 日語 or 日文. Alone, 日 is a bound form that stands for Japan.

column3: 台湾人 is a Taiwanese person. 台湾话 usually means Taiwanese Hokkien, not Mandarin. Mandarin is 国语 in Taiwan, 普通话 on the mainland and 华语 in Southeast Asia; 中文 works everywhere.
column7: I live in Taiwan.
column9: 臺灣人 is a Taiwanese person. 台灣話 usually means Taiwanese Hokkien, not Mandarin. Mandarin is 國語 in Taiwan, 普通話 on the mainland and 華語 in Southeast Asia; 中文 works everywhere.

column3: Older sister. In Taiwan both 姊姊 and 姐姐 are written and both are fine; the mainland writes 姐姐. It is the same word, and in speech many people say jiějie. Younger sister is 妹妹, and for sisters in order people say 大姊, 二姊.
column7: My older sister works at a bank.
column9: Older sister. In Taiwan both 姊姊 and 姐姐 are written and both are fine; the mainland writes 姐姐. It is the same word, and in speech many people say jiějie. Younger sister is 妹妹, and for sisters in order people say 大姊, 二姊.

column3: Older sister. In speech it is often used alone after a pronoun: 我姐 "my sister", 你姐 "your sister" (他姐 is rarer). 姊妹 means "sisters" (older and younger), and 大姊, 二姊 count the sisters in order. Taiwan writes both 姊 and 姐.
column7: They are sisters.
column9: Older sister. In speech it is often used alone after a pronoun: 我姐 "my sister", 你姐 "your sister" (他姐 is rarer). 姊妹 means "sisters" (older and younger), and 大姊, 二姊 count the sisters in order. Taiwan writes both 姊 and 姐.

column3: The usual word for a young child, counted with 个: 两个小孩. It also means one's own children: 你有小孩吗? 小朋友 is the friendlier word to or about children.
column7: That child is very cute.
column9: The usual word for a young child, counted with 個: 兩個小孩. It also means one's own children: 你有小孩嗎? 小朋友 is the friendlier word to or about children.

column3: The same word as 小孩 with the suffix 子, a little more spoken and warmer. It is also used to scold or excuse: 小孩子不懂, "he is only a child, he does not understand". Say 一个小孩子 for one child.
column7: Children shouldn't drink coffee.
column9: The same word as 小孩 with the suffix 子, a little more spoken and warmer. It is also used to scold or excuse: 小孩子不懂, "he is only a child, he does not understand". Say 一個小孩子 for one child.

column3: It is about how long something lasts: 很久, 多久, and 好久不见 for "long time no see". After a verb it comes last: 我等了很久; with a negative it comes first: 很久没见. For the length of an object, use 长, not 久.
column7: I waited a long time.
column9: It is about how long something lasts: 很久, 多久, and 好久不見 for "long time no see". After a verb it comes last: 我等了很久; with a negative it comes first: 很久沒見. For the length of an object, use 長, not 久.

column3: City bus. 公车 is the everyday word in Taiwan, and 公车站 is a bus stop. The mainland says 公交车 or 公共汽车. Take it with 坐: 坐公车 "ride the bus".
column7: I take the bus to school every day.
column9: City bus. 公車 is the everyday word in Taiwan, and 公車站 is a bus stop. The mainland says 公交車 or 公共汽車. Take it with 坐: 坐公車 "ride the bus".

column3: Any vehicle, often a car, and in Taiwan also a scooter or bicycle. It is common in Taiwan and southern China, where northern speech says just 车. The measure word is 辆: 一辆车子.
column6: Tā de chēzi shì hóngsè de.
column7: His car is red.
column9: Any vehicle, often a car, and in Taiwan also a scooter or bicycle. It is common in Taiwan and southern China, where northern speech says just 車. The measure word is 輛: 一輛車子.

column3: Put the verb after it: 容易学, 容易忘. 不容易 often means "difficult", and the opposite is 难. 好不容易 means "with great difficulty", not "very easy".
column7: Chinese is not easy to learn.
column9: Put the verb after it: 容易學, 容易忘. 不容易 often means "difficult", and the opposite is 難. 好不容易 means "with great difficulty", not "very easy".

column3: 礼拜 is the more colloquial word for "week", with a southern flavor (Taiwan, Shanghai, Guangdong), so 礼拜一 is Monday and 两个礼拜 is two weeks. 星期天 and 星期日 mean the same and are standard everywhere.
column7: On Sunday we are going hiking.
column9: 禮拜 is the more colloquial word for "week", with a southern flavor (Taiwan, Shanghai, Guangdong), so 禮拜一 is Monday and 兩個禮拜 is two weeks. 星期天 and 星期日 mean the same and are standard everywhere.

column3: It is blunt: telling an adult 你胖了 is impolite in most company, so use it of yourself or a pet. 变胖 means "get fat" and the opposite is 瘦. For fat on meat the word is 肥.
column7: He has gotten fat lately.
column9: It is blunt: telling an adult 你胖了 is impolite in most company, so use it of yourself or a pet. 變胖 means "get fat" and the opposite is 瘦. For fat on meat the word is 肥.

column3: The opposite of 高 for people, buildings and plants: 他比我矮. A short length of something is 短, not 矮. 矮子 is an insulting word for a short person; avoid it.
column7: My younger brother is shorter than me.
column9: The opposite of 高 for people, buildings and plants: 他比我矮. A short length of something is 短, not 矮. 矮子 is an insulting word for a short person; avoid it.

column3: The opposite of 胖, and not rude: 你好瘦 is fine to say. With 了 it shows change, 瘦了 "have lost weight". It also describes meat: 瘦肉 is lean meat.
column7: She is both tall and thin.
column9: The opposite of 胖, and not rude: 你好瘦 is fine to say. With 了 it shows change, 瘦了 "have lost weight". It also describes meat: 瘦肉 is lean meat.

column3: The colloquial word for an hour as a length of time, counted with 个: 两个钟头, 半个钟头. 小时 is the standard word and means the same. For a time on the clock use 点: 三点.
column6: Wǒ děng le liǎng ge zhōngtóu.
column7: I waited two hours.
column9: The colloquial word for an hour as a length of time, counted with 個: 兩個鐘頭, 半個鐘頭. 小時 is the standard word and means the same. For a time on the clock use 點: 三點.

column3: The row of year words goes 前年, 去年, 今年, 明年, 后年. Like other time words it goes before the verb or first in the sentence. It is a fixed year, unlike 后来 "later".
column7: I will go to Taiwan the year after next.
column9: The row of year words goes 前年, 去年, 今年, 明年, 後年. Like other time words it goes before the verb or first in the sentence. It is a fixed year, unlike 後來 "later".

column3: Used for looks and scenery: 风景很美, 她很美. Longer words are 美丽 and 漂亮, and it is the first character of 美国.
column7: The scenery here is beautiful.
column9: Used for looks and scenery: 風景很美, 她很美. Longer words are 美麗 and 漂亮, and it is the first character of 美國.

column3: Found mostly in 应该, which goes before the verb: 你应该早点睡. 不应该 means "should not".
column6: Nǐ yīng gāi zǎo yī diǎn shuì.
column7: You should go to bed earlier.
column9: Found mostly in 應該, which goes before the verb: 你應該早點睡. 不應該 means "should not".

column3: A title: in Taiwan 王医师 is the usual way to say Dr. Wang, while on the mainland it is 王医生 or 王大夫. 医生 is the everyday word for a doctor on both sides. 师 also ends titles such as 老师.
column7: This doctor is very kind.
column9: A title: in Taiwan 王醫師 is the usual way to say Dr. Wang, while on the mainland it is 王醫生 or 王大夫. 醫生 is the everyday word for a doctor on both sides. 師 also ends titles such as 老師.

column3: For an amount: 一点水, 吃一点. After an adjective it softens a comparison or request: 大一点, 便宜一点.
column7: I'd like to drink a little water.
column9: For an amount: 一點水, 吃一點. After an adjective it softens a comparison or request: 大一點, 便宜一點.

column3: The measure word for flat things that spread out: 一张纸, 两张票, 一张桌子, 一张床, and photographs. It is also a very common surname.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng piào.
column7: I bought two tickets.
column9: The measure word for flat things that spread out: 一張紙, 兩張票, 一張桌子, 一張床, and photographs. It is also a very common surname.

column3: Usually a larger sit-down place with a menu, or a hotel's dining room. 餐馆 and 饭馆 are also used, and 小吃店 is a small eatery. The measure word is 家: 一家餐厅. 厅 also appears in 客厅 "living room".
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food at this restaurant is very good.
column9: Usually a larger sit-down place with a menu, or a hotel's dining room. 餐館 and 飯館 are also used, and 小吃店 is a small eatery. The measure word is 家: 一家餐廳. 廳 also appears in 客廳 "living room".

column3: Read aloud and "study". In Taiwan 念书 means "study, go to school", and 念大学 "attend university". For reading a text aloud, Taiwan writes 念 or 念, and both are fine. For "miss someone", only 念 is used: 想念你. The thing read comes after: 念课文 "read the text aloud".
column7: Please read this character aloud.
column9: Read aloud and "study". In Taiwan 念書 means "study, go to school", and 念大學 "attend university". For reading a text aloud, Taiwan writes 念 or 唸, and both are fine. For "miss someone", only 念 is used: 想念你. The thing read comes after: 念課文 "read the text aloud".

column3: The measure word for long thin things, above all pens and flowers: 一枝笔, 一枝花. Taiwan commonly writes 枝 here, where the mainland usually writes 支.
column7: I have two pens.
column9: The measure word for long thin things, above all pens and flowers: 一枝筆, 一枝花. Taiwan commonly writes 枝 here, where the mainland usually writes 支.

column3: It is the base of 牛肉 "beef", 牛奶 "milk" and 牛肉面. The measure word is 头: 一头牛. As slang it also means "awesome": 你真牛.
column7: This cow is very big.
column9: It is the base of 牛肉 "beef", 牛奶 "milk" and 牛肉麵. The measure word is 頭: 一頭牛. As slang it also means "awesome": 你真牛.

column3: 猪肉 is pork. The measure word is 头: 一头猪, as for other livestock; 只 is also heard. A pig is also an insult for a greedy or lazy person, so do not call someone 猪.
column7: That pig is very fat.
column9: 豬肉 is pork. The measure word is 頭: 一頭豬, as for other livestock; 隻 is also heard. A pig is also an insult for a greedy or lazy person, so do not call someone 豬.

column3: In Taiwan 功课 is the everyday word for homework: 写功课, 做功课. On the mainland homework is 作业, and 功课 leans toward schoolwork and lessons. It is not for a job, which is 工作.
column7: I haven't finished my homework yet.
column9: In Taiwan 功課 is the everyday word for homework: 寫功課, 做功課. On the mainland homework is 作業, and 功課 leans toward schoolwork and lessons. It is not for a job, which is 工作.

column3: Mostly part of a longer word: 房间 "room", 房子 "house, apartment", 房租 "rent", 房东 "landlord". On its own it appears in signs and set phrases more than in speech. 房子 is the everyday word for a home you buy or rent.
column6: Wǒ zài fáng lǐ kàn shū.
column7: I am reading in my room.
column9: Mostly part of a longer word: 房間 "room", 房子 "house, apartment", 房租 "rent", 房東 "landlord". On its own it appears in signs and set phrases more than in speech. 房子 is the everyday word for a home you buy or rent.

column3: Almost always in 桌子, or in 书桌 "desk" and 餐桌 "dining table". 张 is the measure word for a table: 一张桌子. Alone, 桌 counts tables of guests or dishes at a meal: 一桌菜.
column6: Wǒmen diǎn le yī zhuō cài.
column7: We ordered a whole table of dishes.
column9: Almost always in 桌子, or in 書桌 "desk" and 餐桌 "dining table". 張 is the measure word for a table: 一張桌子. Alone, 桌 counts tables of guests or dishes at a meal: 一桌菜.

column3: Normally in 椅子, with 张 as the measure word, like a table: 一张椅子. You sit on one with 坐: 坐在椅子上.
column6: Qǐng zuò zài yǐ zi shàng.
column7: Please sit on the chair.
column9: Normally in 椅子, with 張 as the measure word, like a table: 一張椅子. You sit on one with 坐: 坐在椅子上.

column3: Flower, with the spoken ending 儿. That ending is a northern, mainland habit; in Taiwan the word is simply 花, and 花儿 mainly shows up in songs and poems. The measure word is 朵 for a flower, 束 for a bunch, and 枝 for a single stem.
column6: Yuànzi lǐ de huār kāi le.
column7: The flowers in the yard have bloomed.
column9: Flower, with the spoken ending 兒. That ending is a northern, mainland habit; in Taiwan the word is simply 花, and 花兒 mainly shows up in songs and poems. The measure word is 朵 for a flower, 束 for a bunch, and 枝 for a single stem.

column3: 咖啡店 and 咖啡厅 are cafés. Count it with 杯: 一杯咖啡; the verb is 喝咖啡.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng hē yī bēi kāfēi.
column7: I'd like a cup of coffee.
column9: 咖啡店 and 咖啡廳 are cafés. Count it with 杯: 一杯咖啡; the verb is 喝咖啡.

column3: It is followed by a measure word or time word: 每天, 每个人, 每次. Each + noun often goes with 都 later in the sentence: 每个人都来了.
column6: Měi ge rén dōu lái le.
column7: Everyone came.
column9: It is followed by a measure word or time word: 每天, 每個人, 每次. Each + noun often goes with 都 later in the sentence: 每個人都來了.

column3: For leisure, not sports: 去哪里玩, 玩游戏, 好玩. 来我家玩 means "come over". You can also play with objects: 玩手机. Ball games take 打 or 踢, not 玩.
column6: Zhōumò nǐ xiǎng qù nǎlǐ wán?
column7: Where do you want to go for fun this weekend?
column9: For leisure, not sports: 去哪裡玩, 玩遊戲, 好玩. 來我家玩 means "come over". You can also play with objects: 玩手機. Ball games take 打 or 踢, not 玩.

column3: 跳高 is the high jump, 跳起来 "jump up". It is the first half of 跳舞 "dance", and 心跳 is a heartbeat. Degree comes after 得: 他跳得很高.
column7: He jumps very high.
column9: 跳高 is the high jump, 跳起來 "jump up". It is the first half of 跳舞 "dance", and 心跳 is a heartbeat. Degree comes after 得: 他跳得很高.

column3: A verb plus object, so a degree repeats the verb: 跳舞跳得很好, or 舞跳得很好. One dance is counted with 支: 跳一支舞.
column7: She likes dancing very much.
column9: A verb plus object, so a degree repeats the verb: 跳舞跳得很好, or 舞跳得很好. One dance is counted with 支: 跳一支舞.

column3: Thing, matter, with the northern 儿 ending, common on the mainland. Taiwan says 事 or 事情: 有事 "have something to do", 没事 "nothing's wrong". 你有什么事儿吗 sounds northern or mainland to Taiwan ears; in Taiwan you would more likely hear 你有什么事吗.
column7: Is there something you need?
column9: Thing, matter, with the northern 兒 ending, common on the mainland. Taiwan says 事 or 事情: 有事 "have something to do", 沒事 "nothing's wrong". 你有什麼事兒嗎 sounds northern or mainland to Taiwan ears; in Taiwan you would more likely hear 你有什麼事嗎.

column3: It follows the place: 房间里面, often shortened to 房间里. On its own it can start a sentence as the place: 里面有人吗? The opposite is 外面.
column7: There is money in the wallet.
column9: It follows the place: 房間裡面, often shortened to 房間裡. On its own it can start a sentence as the place: 裡面有人嗎? The opposite is 外面.

column3: It follows the place: 桌子上面, or the shorter 桌子上. In writing it can mean above-mentioned, as in 上面说的. It forms a set with 下面, 里面 and 外面.
column7: The book is on the table.
column9: It follows the place: 桌子上面, or the shorter 桌子上. In writing it can mean above-mentioned, as in 上面說的. It forms a set with 下面, 裡面 and 外面.

column3: It follows the place: 椅子下面, or the shorter 桌子下. It also means what comes next in a text or talk: 下面请看 means please look at what follows.
column7: The cat is under the chair.
column9: It follows the place: 椅子下面, or the shorter 桌子下. It also means what comes next in a text or talk: 下面請看 means please look at what follows.

column3: The usual word for outside: 外面很冷, 在外面等. The spoken variant is 外头. It also means away from home, as in 在外面吃饭 for eating out.
column7: It is raining outside.
column9: The usual word for outside: 外面很冷, 在外面等. The spoken variant is 外頭. It also means away from home, as in 在外面吃飯 for eating out.

column3: The more colloquial twin of 外面: 外头很冷, 在外头等. The same light 头 gives 里头, 前头 and 后头.
column6: Wàitou hěn lěng, duō chuān yīdiǎn.
column7: It's cold outside, wear more.
column9: The more colloquial twin of 外面: 外頭很冷, 在外頭等. The same light 頭 gives 裡頭, 前頭 and 後頭.

column3: It names the place ahead or in front: 前面有一家店. In a text or talk it means the part earlier on: 前面提到过. The opposite is 后面. 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.
column7: There is a restaurant ahead.
column9: It names the place ahead or in front: 前面有一家店. In a text or talk it means the part earlier on: 前面提到過. The opposite is 後面. 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.

column3: Besides place (在公园后面), it means the part that comes later: 后面还有. The opposite is 前面.
column7: The school is behind the park.
column9: Besides place (在公園後面), it means the part that comes later: 後面還有. The opposite is 前面.

column3: It lives in compounds: 旁边 next to, 路旁 roadside, 旁人 bystanders. It is also the word for a side component of a character, as in 偏旁.
column6: Lù páng yǒu yī kē dà shù.
column7: There is a big tree by the roadside.
column9: It lives in compounds: 旁邊 next to, 路旁 roadside, 旁人 bystanders. It is also the word for a side component of a character, as in 偏旁.

column3: Place. It takes a describing word before it: 好地方 "a good place", 什么地方 "what place", 这个地方 "this place". 你住什么地方？ "where do you live?" is a question with it, though 哪里 is the more common question word.
column7: This place is very quiet.
column9: Place. It takes a describing word before it: 好地方 "a good place", 什麼地方 "what place", 這個地方 "this place". 你住什麼地方？ "where do you live?" is a question with it, though 哪裡 is the more common question word.

column3: It follows the place: 学校附近, or stands alone as in 这附近 for around here. It also modifies a noun: 附近的商店. It covers an area, not an exact distance.
column7: Is there a bank around here?
column9: It follows the place: 學校附近, or stands alone as in 這附近 for around here. It also modifies a noun: 附近的商店. It covers an area, not an exact distance.

column3: Taxi, the standard word in Taiwan. It is made of 计程 "measure the distance" and 车, for the meter; the mainland says 出租车, and Hong Kong 的士. Cabs in Taiwan are famous yellow, and people often call them 小黄. You take one with 坐 and call one with 叫: 叫计程车.
column7: Let's go by taxi.
column9: Taxi, the standard word in Taiwan. It is made of 計程 "measure the distance" and 車, for the meter; the mainland says 出租車, and Hong Kong 的士. Cabs in Taiwan are famous yellow, and people often call them 小黃. You take one with 坐 and call one with 叫: 叫計程車.

column3: Nose, mostly in compounds, with 鼻子 the word used alone. With a cold, 流鼻水 is a runny nose and 鼻塞 a stuffy nose. 鼻涕 is the thicker snot; Taiwan uses both words, for different things.
column7: My nose keeps running.
column9: Nose, mostly in compounds, with 鼻子 the word used alone. With a cold, 流鼻水 is a runny nose and 鼻塞 a stuffy nose. 鼻涕 is the thicker snot; Taiwan uses both words, for different things.

column3: The everyday word for nose, with the suffix 子. 鼻 alone turns up in compounds such as 鼻塞 for a stuffy nose. 自 was the original character for nose, but it came to mean self, so 鼻 took over the sense of nose.
column7: She has a high-bridged nose.
column9: The everyday word for nose, with the suffix 子. 鼻 alone turns up in compounds such as 鼻塞 for a stuffy nose. 自 was the original character for nose, but it came to mean self, so 鼻 took over the sense of nose.

column3: Count one ear with 只 and a pair with 对. Body parts take 的 or not: 我的耳朵. 朵 also counts flowers and clouds: 一朵花. Earache is 耳朵痛.
column7: My ear hurts a lot.
column9: Count one ear with 隻 and a pair with 對. Body parts take 的 or not: 我的耳朵. 朵 also counts flowers and clouds: 一朵花. Earache is 耳朵痛.

column3: It is both verb and noun: 我感冒了, 得了感冒, and 感冒药 for the medicine. On the mainland it is also used, mostly negated, for "interested": 我对打球不感冒 means ball games don't interest me. In Taiwan 感冒 by itself can mean to detest.
column6: Wǒ gǎnmào le, tóu hěn tòng.
column7: I have a cold and my head hurts a lot.
column9: It is both verb and noun: 我感冒了, 得了感冒, and 感冒藥 for the medicine. On the mainland it is also used, mostly negated, for "interested": 我對打球不感冒 means ball games don't interest me. In Taiwan 感冒 by itself can mean to detest.

column3: The usual word for hurt in Taiwan: 头痛, 肚子痛, 好痛. In northern mainland speech 疼 is common, though 痛 is understood. The body part comes first: 我的肚子痛.
column7: My stomach hurts a lot.
column9: The usual word for hurt in Taiwan: 頭痛, 肚子痛, 好痛. In northern mainland speech 疼 is common, though 痛 is understood. The body part comes first: 我的肚子痛.

column3: The spoken noun for mouth; 嘴 alone is common in compounds such as 嘴唇, 闭嘴. The formal word is 口. Informally it stands for speech: 嘴巴很甜 means sweet-talking. 巴 here is a nominalizing suffix, as in 尾巴.
column7: Please open your mouth.
column9: The spoken noun for mouth; 嘴 alone is common in compounds such as 嘴唇, 閉嘴. The formal word is 口. Informally it stands for speech: 嘴巴很甜 means sweet-talking. 巴 here is a nominalizing suffix, as in 尾巴.

column3: Count a pair with 双: 一双鞋子; 一只 is a single shoe. 鞋 ends many names: 运动鞋, 拖鞋, 皮鞋. Shoes come off at the door: 请脱鞋子.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī shuāng xīn xiézi.
column7: I want to buy a new pair of shoes.
column9: Count a pair with 雙: 一雙鞋子; 一隻 is a single shoe. 鞋 ends many names: 運動鞋, 拖鞋, 皮鞋. Shoes come off at the door: 請脫鞋子.

column3: It does not stand alone in speech but sits in compounds: 衣服 with the measure word 件, 上衣 for a top, 雨衣 for a raincoat.
column4: 衣食住行是生活的基本需要。
column5: 衣食住行是生活的基本需要。
column6: Yī shí zhù xíng shì shēnghuó de jīběn xūyào.
column7: Clothing, food, housing and transport are the basic needs of life.
column9: It does not stand alone in speech but sits in compounds: 衣服 with the measure word 件, 上衣 for a top, 雨衣 for a raincoat.

column3: It is for things, not for people's age, which is 老: 旧衣服, 旧朋友, 旧地方. The opposite is 新.
column6: Zhè shuāng xiézi tài jiù le.
column7: This pair of shoes is too old.
column9: It is for things, not for people's age, which is 老: 舊衣服, 舊朋友, 舊地方. The opposite is 新.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 一共 for the total (before the verb or number), 共同 for joint, 公共 for public. Alone it is formal writing.
column6: Wǒmen gòng yǒu sān gè rén.
column7: There are three of us in all.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 一共 for the total (before the verb or number), 共同 for joint, 公共 for public. Alone it is formal writing.

column3: Chopsticks, in 筷子, always plural in use: 一双筷子 "a pair of chopsticks". The older word for chopsticks was 箸, which sounded like 住 "stay, stop", so the name was avoided and 快 "fast" gave the new one. 用筷子吃饭 "eat with chopsticks".
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī shuāng kuàizi.
column7: Please give me a pair of chopsticks.
column9: Chopsticks, in 筷子, always plural in use: 一雙筷子 "a pair of chopsticks". The older word for chopsticks was 箸, which sounded like 住 "stay, stop", so the name was avoided and 快 "fast" gave the new one. 用筷子吃飯 "eat with chopsticks".

column3: It goes before an adjective, usually an unwelcome one: 有点贵, 有点冷. After the adjective, 一点 compares: 贵一点 is a bit pricier, and 便宜一点吧 softens a request. Before a verb: 我有点想家.
column7: This is a bit expensive.
column9: It goes before an adjective, usually an unwelcome one: 有點貴, 有點冷. After the adjective, 一點 compares: 貴一點 is a bit pricier, and 便宜一點吧 softens a request. Before a verb: 我有點想家.

column3: Interchangeable with 有点 before an adjective, again usually unwelcome: 有一点饿. Before a noun it is literal: 我有一点钱 means I have a bit of money.
column7: I am a little hungry.
column9: Interchangeable with 有點 before an adjective, again usually unwelcome: 有一點餓. Before a noun it is literal: 我有一點錢 means I have a bit of money.

column3: Cheap dishes sold at stalls and markets, such as 小笼包 and 煎饼. 小吃店 is a small eatery serving them. Packaged snacks are 零食.
column7: The night market has a lot of snacks.
column9: Cheap dishes sold at stalls and markets, such as 小籠包 and 煎餅. 小吃店 is a small eatery serving them. Packaged snacks are 零食.

column3: Usually part of a compound: 饺子, 水饺 for boiled dumplings, 锅贴 for pan-fried ones. To eat them: 吃水饺. 饺 comes from 角, horn, named for its horn-like shape.
column6: Wǒmen wǎnshang bāo jiǎo zi ba.
column7: Let's make dumplings tonight.
column9: Usually part of a compound: 餃子, 水餃 for boiled dumplings, 鍋貼 for pan-fried ones. To eat them: 吃水餃. 餃 comes from 角, horn, named for its horn-like shape.

column3: In Chinese soup is drunk, 喝汤, and counted by the bowl: 一碗汤. Soups are named by their contents: 蛋花汤, 鱼汤.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng hē yī wǎn rè tāng.
column7: I'd like a bowl of hot soup.
column9: In Chinese soup is drunk, 喝湯, and counted by the bowl: 一碗湯. Soups are named by their contents: 蛋花湯, 魚湯.

column3: 生日蛋糕 is a birthday cake, 一块蛋糕 a piece of it, and 蛋糕店 a cake shop. 糕 alone ends names of steamed foods such as 年糕 and 萝卜糕. 糕 is food made from rice flour.
column7: I want to eat birthday cake.
column9: 生日蛋糕 is a birthday cake, 一塊蛋糕 a piece of it, and 蛋糕店 a cake shop. 糕 alone ends names of steamed foods such as 年糕 and 蘿蔔糕. 糕 is food made from rice flour.

column3: Count a single banana with 根 and a bunch with 串: 吃一根香蕉. 香蕉牛奶 is a common drink.
column4: 我每天早上吃一根香蕉。
column5: 我每天早上吃一根香蕉。
column6: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang chī yī gēn xiāngjiāo.
column7: I eat a banana every morning.
column9: Count a single banana with 根 and a bunch with 串: 吃一根香蕉. 香蕉牛奶 is a common drink.

column3: Drink, beverage. Taiwan's 饮料店 sell tea drinks and are everywhere, like bubble tea shops. Ask 你想喝什么饮料？ for "what do you want to drink?". The mainland says 饮料 too, but also 饮品. Put 喝 in front: 喝饮料. Cold drinks: 冷饮.
column7: What would you like to drink?
column9: Drink, beverage. Taiwan's 飲料店 sell tea drinks and are everywhere, like bubble tea shops. Ask 你想喝什麼飲料？ for "what do you want to drink?". The mainland says 飲料 too, but also 飲品. Put 喝 in front: 喝飲料. Cold drinks: 冷飲.

column3: Count with 杯: 一杯果汁. A specific juice names the fruit first: 苹果汁, 西瓜汁. 汁 alone also appears in 肉汁 for gravy.
column7: I'd like a glass of juice.
column9: Count with 杯: 一杯果汁. A specific juice names the fruit first: 苹果汁, 西瓜汁. 汁 alone also appears in 肉汁 for gravy.

column3: It also describes pleasant, endearing things: 声音很甜, 笑得很甜. Opposite: 苦, and 咸 for salty. In drink shops you pick the sugar: 全糖, 半糖, 微糖, 无糖.
column6: Zhè bēi yǐnliào tài tián le.
column7: This drink is too sweet.
column9: It also describes pleasant, endearing things: 聲音很甜, 笑得很甜. Opposite: 苦, and 鹹 for salty. In drink shops you pick the sugar: 全糖, 半糖, 微糖, 無糖.

column3: It names the food and the drink: 巧克力蛋糕, 热巧克力. Count pieces with 块.
column7: I like eating chocolate.
column9: It names the food and the drink: 巧克力蛋糕, 熱巧克力. Count pieces with 塊.

column3: Ice, and "iced, cold". 冰水 is "ice water" and 冰的 "the cold one". When ordering a drink in Taiwan: 正常冰 "regular ice", 少冰 "less ice", 微冰 "a little ice", 去冰 "no ice". 冰箱 is "refrigerator", and 冰淇淋 "ice cream".
column6: Wǒ yào bīng de, bù yào rè de.
column7: I want the cold one, not the hot one.
column9: Ice, and "iced, cold". 冰水 is "ice water" and 冰的 "the cold one". When ordering a drink in Taiwan: 正常冰 "regular ice", 少冰 "less ice", 微冰 "a little ice", 去冰 "no ice". 冰箱 is "refrigerator", and 冰淇淋 "ice cream".

column3: Side, with the northern ending 儿. In Taiwan people usually say 边 or 旁边, 左边 "left side", 这边 "this side", and keep 边儿 as something heard in northern speech or on the mainland. 路边 is "roadside". The 儿 ending is not written in Taiwan's everyday text.
column7: There is a shop by the road.
column9: Side, with the northern ending 兒. In Taiwan people usually say 邊 or 旁邊, 左邊 "left side", 這邊 "this side", and keep 邊兒 as something heard in northern speech or on the mainland. 路邊 is "roadside". The 兒 ending is not written in Taiwan's everyday text.

column3: Before a verb it means must: 我得走了. The negative is 不用 or 不必, not 不得. The stronger written word is 必须.
column7: I have to go.
column9: Before a verb it means must: 我得走了. The negative is 不用 or 不必, not 不得. The stronger written word is 必須.
